source.title: M3GD: Multi-Modal Multi-View Geometric Diffusion for Camera--LiDAR Novel View Synthesis
source.authors: Yang Zhou; Jiuhong Xiao; Shi-Zhao Ye; Quang Long; Carlos Nieto-Granda; Giuseppe Loianno

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper is present. Some PDF text has layout/line-break artifacts, but the relevant results and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures similarity between independently pretrained image and point-cloud representations using several spatial-structure metrics, a conceptual test of cross-modal representation alignment. It does not test convergence as model scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the representation-similarity measurements in Table I. The NVS quality, ablation, deployment, and runtime results concern the utility of LiDAR conditioning, not convergence between representations. Table I reports macro averages across images; its metric values are extracted below. The paper's statements about cited prior work are not treated as results here.
record.test_reason: The study measures zero-shot representational similarity between independently trained, frozen image encoders (DA3, DINOv2, VGGT) and a point-cloud encoder (Utonia) on shared image-grid cells, using five similarity metrics (Table I). This is a new cross-modal setting (image vs LiDAR, not image vs text) with results on how alignment depends on the metric (V6) and how incomplete it is (V7). There is no scale or capability sweep, so V1 is not tested. It is T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that projected Utonia features share substantial spatial structure with frozen DA3 image features, strongest at level 0 and with DA3 as the best image backbone, without any alignment training. They interpret this as shared spatial structure, not coordinate-wise equivalence, since the image-only reference is stronger on most metrics. They call this consistent with the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, but they do not test scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares projected and pooled point-cloud features with image features on shared supported cells using PCA-aligned channel correlation, linear CKA, SVCCA, Jaccard@10, and affinity-matrix correlation. It is not a scale sweep or a direct reproduction of the original sources' full claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported similarity depends on the metric: DA3–Utonia exceeds the DA3–DINOv2 reference on Jaccard@10 but is lower on the other four metrics. It also varies with DA3 feature level and image-backbone choice; the authors identify level 0 as strongest overall and report weaker raw-feature alignment at higher levels, especially in CKA.

fits_no_version.finding: Independently trained, frozen image encoders and a LiDAR point-cloud encoder (Utonia, trained with no image supervision) show substantial shared spatial structure after camera projection: CKA 0.43–0.66 and PCA correlation of about 0.62–0.64 across backbones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convergence across sensing modalities without language: independently trained 2D image and 3D point-cloud encoders share similarity structure over co-located scene regions without any alignment training.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code and protocols will be released, but gives no URL)
record.problems: The representation study uses one dataset and one robot platform (GrandTour/ANYmal-D); no model-size or capability sweep is reported. Table I gives macro averages but no uncertainty estimates. Only cells with valid projected LiDAR support are compared, and the study does not test out-of-distribution inputs or alternative neighbor counts.
record.rows_left_out: None of the Table I similarity results were omitted. Results from other sections were left out because they evaluate NVS performance, conditioning ablations, or deployment rather than representation convergence.

untested.parts: There is no model-size or capability sweep, so it cannot show whether alignment rises with scale.
There is no vision–language or image–caption comparison. The cross-modal pair is image vs LiDAR point cloud.
There is no comparison across seeds.
No mapping, stitching or interchangeability loss is measured. The NVS adapter is a learned fusion, not a test of mapping quality.
The number of neighbours is fixed at 10, and inputs are not varied out of distribution (a single dataset and robot platform).
There is no plateau-over-scale test, and the study does not test whether shared data or objectives explain the alignment.

record.verdict_notes: Only Table I bears on the claim. The NVS, ablation and runtime results concern downstream utility. No uncertainty is reported for the similarity values. Similarity is computed only on LiDAR-supported cells, which may favour well-structured regions. The V7 'supports' label rests on incompleteness alone, not on causes or plateaus. A reader could alternatively see these values as evidence for substantial convergence, which is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no measurement of whether alignment rises with scale or performance.
No vision-language model comparison or paired image-caption representation test.
No comparison across random seeds of the same architecture.
No test of mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired interchangeability.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
The study varies similarity metrics and feature levels/backbones, but does not vary neighbor count or input distributions and does not report an out-of-distribution similarity test.
It compares cross-modal similarity with an image-only reference, but does not test plateauing over scale or whether shared training data/objectives cause the measured alignment.

relationships.condition: Table I: DA3 levels 0–3, three image backbones, and the image-only reference, each scored on five metrics
relationships.reason: Rankings flip with the metric. DA3 level-3 is top on PCA correlation and Jaccard but lowest on CKA and affinity (r16–r20). VGGT matches DA3 on PCA but is far lower on CKA and affinity (r26–r30 vs r01–r05). The cross-modal pair equals the image-only reference on Jaccard but trails it on the other four metrics (r01–r05 vs r31–r35).
relationships.display_finding: DA3 level-3 ranked highest on PCA correlation and Jaccard but lowest on CKA and affinity, while VGGT matched DA3 on PCA but scored far lower on CKA and affinity; the cross-modal pair matched the image-only reference on Jaccard but trailed it on the other four metrics.

relationships.condition: DA3 level-0 vs Utonia, the best cross-modal pair, compared with the DA3 vs DINOv2 image-only reference
relationships.reason: Even the best cross-modal alignment is moderate (CKA 0.659, SVCCA 0.604, Jaccard 0.355) and below the image-only reference on four of five metrics. The authors state it is not coordinate-wise equivalence (r01–r05, r31–r35).
relationships.display_finding: DA3–Utonia reached CKA 0.659, SVCCA 0.604 and Jaccard 0.355, falling below DA3–DINOv2 on four of five metrics without coordinate-wise equivalence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Compared similarity measures and feature pairs in Table I
reader_labels.reason: The measures do not give identical relative comparisons: DA3–Utonia slightly exceeds the image-only reference on Jaccard@10 (r04 vs r34), while the image-only reference is higher on PCA correlation, CKA, SVCCA, and affinity correlation (r01–r03, r05 vs r31–r33, r35).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: DA3-Base level-0–Utonia compared with the DA3-Base level-0–DINOv2 reference
reader_labels.reason: The authors characterize cross-modal structure as substantial, but it is below the image-only reference on four of five reported metrics; Jaccard@10 is the exception. This supports a qualified, not equivalent, alignment claim (r01–r05, r31–r35).
